input.quote: 8.1 By Commerce One. Commerce One shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Corio and its Customers from any and all damages, liabilities, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees) incurred by Corio or its Customers arising out of any claim that the Software infringes any patent, copyright, trademark or trade right secret of a third party
input.rationale: Section 8.1 gives us (Corio, as licensee/customer) a full defend-and-indemnify from Commerce One (the vendor/licensor) covering third-party claims that the Software infringes patent, copyright, trademark or trade secret rights, and extends to our Customers. It carries the standard procedure (prompt notice, tender of control/defence and settlement to Commerce One at its expense, our cooperation at its expense, with a right to join with our own counsel) and the usual remedy ladder in Section 8.1/p0087 (procure the right, replace or modify, or terminate and refund a pro-rated portion of fees paid). The Section 8.2 exclusions (use other than as documented; third-party modification where the infringement would not have occurred but for the modification) are the usual customer-modification/specification carve-outs. There is no reciprocal Corio indemnity anywhere in the agreement, so the one-way structure runs in our favour, and Section 9 expressly carves "LIABILITY ARISING UNDER SECTION 8" out of both the 12-month fee cap and the consequential-damages exclusion, leaving the vendor indemnity uncapped — better than the fallback's 3x annual fees super-cap. The clause therefore meets the fallback (and on the cap point exceeds it). Noted but not flagged as deviations: the indemnity is limited to IP infringement and does not extend to Commerce One's breach of applicable law, unauthorised access to or disclosure of our data, or its gross negligence/wilful misconduct as the preferred position would provide; the refund remedy is limited to a pro-rated portion of fees paid. These are sub-elements short of preferred wording, not material failures of the fallback, so no redline is proposed.
